clue.text: In Spain, hand a letter to a Greek and use a grand residence

parts.note: mano is the Spanish word for hand
rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a Spanish courtier: pass a note to a Greek visitor and make yourself at home in the mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor house is the large country home of an estate's lord, a grand residence by definition.

clue.text: Pole going around Russian city? That's someone just looking to get hurt

definitions.text: someone just looking to get hurt

indicators.note: going around something means encircling it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a mast is a tall pole on a ship
Sochi is a Black Sea resort, host of the 2014 Winter Olympics

explanation.surface: A Polish visitor travelling round a Russian city, judged to be asking for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a person from Poland, but it is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A masochist takes pleasure in suffering, so seeks out being hurt.

clue.text: Embarrassingly "naturel," like the Swiss

indicators.note: something done embarrassingly is botched, so the letters come out in a muddle

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Swiss people caught au naturel, to their embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: Au naturel is French for naked, a nod to the 17 theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Switzerland is famous for staying neutral, taking no side in wars.

clue.text: Spoken version of appropriate ceremony

indicators.note: a spoken version is what the ear hears, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: right means appropriate or fitting

explanation.surface: A spoken form of a fitting ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal religious or solemn ceremony.

clue.text: Discover French city held in reserve

parts.note: split as disc over: a disc is round, the shape of the letter O, and over sets it on top of the next piece in a down entry
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Finding a French town that has been kept back for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discover' looks like one word but splits into disc and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put on ice is set aside or postponed for later use, an idiom from food kept cold.

clue.text: Archetypally, fries and dies?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the classic extra dish ordered with a main course
second meaning, cryptic: the letters of the word side put in a new order spell dies

explanation.surface: Fried potatoes and some other plural, offered as typical examples.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a joke: an 'order' of side is a rearrangement of it, and dies is one.
explanation.definitionFit: French fries are the stock accompaniment ordered alongside a burger, the typical extra dish.

clue.text: Melt what? That's not acceptable

indicators.note: an objection that the word as given will not do, so its letters must be put in another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to melt something replies in disbelief and refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'what?' read as an outburst, but it is the raw material: WHAT, with its letters reordered, is THAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To thaw is to warm from a frozen state into liquid, a synonym for melting.

clue.text: Something you might see in the front hall or hear on a sitcom?

definitions.text: Something you might see in the front hall
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stand of pegs for hats near the door
second meaning, by sound: a recorded track of 'ha' laughter, a laugh track

explanation.walkthrough: Split as ha track, the word describes the canned laughter dubbed onto a sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatrack is furniture with pegs for headgear, standing in an entrance hall.

clue.text: Brief message about the origin of life in the universe

indicators.note: about here means around, so the message wraps the selected letter

parts.note: to send word is to send a short message

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of life

explanation.surface: A short note on how life began in the cosmos.
explanation.definitionFit: World can mean all of creation, everything that exists, as in 'the whole world'.

clue.text: Nothing is short and thick

definitions.meaning: first meaning: American slang for nothing at all
second meaning: stocky, low and broad in build

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark that nothing is ever both brief and dense.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat is US slang for nothing whatsoever, and as an adjective describes a dumpy, stocky shape.

clue.text: Signal heard in Illinois city — and "heard" in this clue

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound, so the next words are spoken and spelt as they sound

parts.note: Decatur is a city in Illinois; said quickly, the phrase with in before it gives the word

explanation.surface: A clue that talks about itself: a sound picked up in a Midwestern town, and the word heard sitting in the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is self-referential: the word 'heard' in this very clue is a homophone INDICATOR, the term crossword solvers use for such signal words.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicator is a sign or pointer, and in cryptic jargon it is the word telling the solver which device to apply.

clue.text: Virtuosic musical displays and wild dances, circling the borders of Zambia

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the rearranged letters enclose the edge letters
wild suggests uncontrolled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the borders of a country are its edges, so only its first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of Zambia

explanation.surface: An African music festival with showy solos and frenzied dancing ringing the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is an elaborate solo passage, often improvised, showing off a performer's skill in a concerto.

clue.text: Either could appear instead of F as a kind of degree stopper

wordplay.words: Either could appear instead of F as a kind of degree
wordplay.note: degrees can be F (Fahrenheit), C (Celsius) or K (Kelvin)

explanation.surface: A puzzle about temperature scales: which letters might stand in for the F in degrees Fahrenheit.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the phrase 'C or K', read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork is a plug, typically for a bottle, so it is a type of stopper.

clue.text: Part of a watch is not new

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pointer that sweeps round marking seconds

explanation.surface: A watch repairer noting that one component is a used replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: The second hand is a watch's fastest pointer, and secondhand goods have already had an owner.

clue.text: Yankee airmen flying outside California

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, so they enclose the state abbreviation
flying suggests letters scattered in the air and coming down in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CA is the US postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: US Air Force pilots on a sortie beyond the West Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is a nickname for a person from the United States, especially to foreigners.

clue.text: I criticize a terrible city in Asia

parts.note: taken as written
to slam is to criticize harshly
taken as written
bad means terrible

explanation.surface: A traveller confessing a low opinion of some Asian metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like a description of the city, but it supplies the last chunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, a city in Asia.

clue.text: Like an old TV, with tag and half of that capacity

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one end of it, dropping the rest

parts.note: old televisions were B and W, black and white
an ID tag identifies its wearer
taken as written, then cut in two

explanation.surface: Describing a vintage television set, its label and its reduced power.
explanation.walkthrough: B and W is the usual shorthand for black-and-white; the ampersand-free spelling gives B, AND, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandwidth is the data a connection can carry, so it measures a channel's capacity.

clue.text: Bald school administrator embezzling $1,000 in setback

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the official's title is read from right to left
someone embezzling pockets money, so the official takes the sum inside

parts.note: a dean heads a college or school faculty
K stands for a thousand, as in $5K

explanation.surface: A news story about a hairless college official caught stealing a thousand dollars and suffering a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: The dean is turned round first, then the thousand goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bald can mean bare and unadorned, as in a bald statement, which is what naked means too.

clue.text: Barman's cleanser?

parts.note: surface reading: the soap a bartender uses to wash glasses; setter's reading: a man who bars, that is a gent who deters, so the word splits as deter plus gent

explanation.walkthrough: The bar is not a pub: a barman is someone who bars the way, a deterring gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent such as washing-up liquid, a synonym for cleanser.

clue.text: Regressive attempt to discredit a vegetable

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to rebut is to argue against and try to disprove

explanation.surface: A political smear campaign that turns out to be a backward step, aimed at a veggie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber, such as a potato or yam, is a swollen underground stem eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: "Straight shot"—could you use it in a sentence, or give the language of origin please?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the most direct route somewhere

definitions.text: could you use it in a sentence, or give the language of origin please?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: a line a contestant says at a spelling bee

explanation.surface: A spelling-contest entrant handed the phrase straight shot, asking the usual questions.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling bee contestants may ask for a word's use in a sentence or its origin, so such a request is a line spoken at a bee: a bee line.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a beeline is to go directly somewhere, as a bee supposedly flies straight home.

clue.text: Pest from army's flanks in ravaged, war-torn surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings go all round something, so one group of letters encloses the other
something ravaged has been wrecked, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: the flanks of something are its two sides, so only the end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of army

explanation.surface: Vermin escaping from soldiers in a devastated combat zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norway rat is the common brown rat, a widespread rodent pest.

clue.text: Renaissance instrument in Baroque air? Italians will eat it up

indicators.note: in places the instrument inside the reworked letters
baroque means ornate and convoluted, so the letters are twisted into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the viol is a bowed string instrument of the Renaissance

explanation.surface: An early-music concert where Italians lap up an aria for viol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli is a stuffed pasta dish beloved in Italy, so Italians eat it eagerly.

clue.text: Composer-playwright is distressingly wan-colored

indicators.note: distress implies being upset or thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried note that an artist looks sickly and pale.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward wrote plays such as Private Lives and also songs like 'Mad Dogs and Englishmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward was an English dramatist who also composed and wrote lyrics, so both labels apply.

clue.text: Nosy, like the rapper behind Illmatic?

parts.note: Nas released the album Illmatic in 1994
the suffix -al turns a noun into an adjective meaning like it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an inquisitive person resembles a famous hip-hop artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as Nas-al, 'resembling Nas'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, a jokey sense of nosy.

clue.text: Vaquero, perhaps, at heart!

indicators.note: at heart points into the middle of the phrase, where the word lies concealed

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A claim that a Mexican cattle herder is, deep down, just that.
explanation.walkthrough: A vaquero is a Spanish-speaking cowboy, and the phrase both defines and contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roper is a cowhand skilled with the lasso, which is what a vaquero typically is.

clue.text: State grotto 17

indicators.note: 17 is the entry meaning stripped bare, so the word loses its outer covering of first and last letters

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave or cavern

explanation.surface: A terse note: a cave left in its natural condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 17-across is NAKED, used here as an instruction: strip the cavern of its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly, one sense of state as a verb.

clue.text: Exist on a field

parts.note: are is a form of the verb to be, meaning exist
taken as written

explanation.surface: Living out in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a field of study or activity, as in an area of expertise.

clue.text: Plunge 17 in low-fat guacamole, maybe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a swim without a costume, 17 being the entry for unclothed
second meaning: a lean version of a party dip, read whimsically

explanation.surface: Jumping into a bowl of diet avocado sauce in the altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 17-across is NAKED. Skinny is US slang for low-fat, as in a skinny latte, so guacamole made that way is a skinny dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinny-dip is a swim in the nude, and the second reading treats the phrase as a slimmed-down snack.

clue.text: Listen to reddish French river

indicators.note: an instruction to attend to the sound rather than the spelling of the next word

parts.note: roan is a reddish-brown coat colour of horses

explanation.surface: Someone urged to hear the sound of a rust-coloured stream in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône flows from Switzerland through Lyon to the Mediterranean, a major river of France.

clue.text: Rewind part of movie for a sidelong look

indicators.note: rewinding runs a tape or film backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a reel is one spool of a film

explanation.surface: A film editor running back a scene to catch a sly glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewind' fits the movie picture so well that it hides its job as the turnaround signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a sly, suggestive glance out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Broadcast Farm Aid for a drug dealer?

indicators.note: a broadcast is listened to, so the phrase is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: aid means assist; said aloud, farm assist matches the word

explanation.surface: A televised benefit concert for farmers, somehow raising money for a narcotics trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Farm Aid is a long-running US benefit concert for family farmers. The question mark flags that 'drug dealer' is meant innocently.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines legally, so is jokingly a dealer in drugs.
